en: The Śrī Mṛtyuñjaya Mental Worship Hymn (Śrīmṛtyuñjayamānasikapūjāstotra)

I meditate upon this Mṛtyuñjaya, who dwells at the foot of a wish-fulfilling tree on Mount Kailāsa, which is inlaid with lovely jewels; whose body is as beautiful as camphor, crystal, and the moon; who is served by Kātyāyanī; whose mass of matted hair is colored by the lofty waves of the Gaṅgā; who is an ocean of compassion; and whose neck is adorned with the serpent Śeṣa as an ornament.
(1) O Mṛtyuñjaya, moon-crested one, adorned with a tiger skin, wielder of the trident, having arrived—
O Lord of the Universe, O Consort of Pārvatī, be gracious like a wish-fulfilling cow to those who are devoted to you.

O All-pervading Lord, remain steadfast upon your glorious lion-throne of rubies, which is adorned with radiant pearl arches and ten thousand emerald pillars; which is perfumed with incense, fashioned of jewels, and illuminated by ruby lamps; and which is graced by hosts of Brahmā, Indra, the gods, and eminent yogis, as well as by celestial wish-granting trees.
Offer the supreme *pādya* for Mṛtyuñjaya with water scented with camphor and *pāṭīra*, and enriched with *mandāra*, *mallī*, *karavīra*, *mādhavī*, *puṇnāga*, *nīlotpala*, and *campaka* flowers.
[5] With auspicious, fragrant heaps of flowers and the cool waters of the celestial river (*Gaṅgā*), [6]...
O Lord of the Three Worlds, dispeller of suffering, honored by all, O Conqueror of Death, please accept this respectful offering.
(5) O Great God, Conqueror of Death, perform the pure ritual rinsing with these cool, most purifying waters, scented with snow-water. (6)

O Three-eyed One, O Destroyer of Death, O One Honored by the Three Worlds, bring forth the auspicious *madhuparka*—consisting of jaggery, curd, honey, excellent clarified butter, and cow’s milk. O you whose five faces are pacified by the five weapons, O Destroyer of the five great sins! 7.

O Lord, O Conqueror of Death, perform this bath with the five nectars (pañcāmṛta). O you who are renowned throughout the three worlds, perform this auspicious bath with waters gathered from all sacred fords (tīrtha) that remove all impurities—O Conqueror of Death, you who delight in infinite virtues! 8–9.

O Lord Śiva, conqueror of death, I cleanse your mass of matted hair with an exceedingly pure silk cloth brought from the celestial tree. I also offer you garments of fine Chinese silk and rags variegated with various gold ornaments.
And hold fast, O Mṛtyuñjaya, to these various divine [attire].
O Mṛtyuñjaya, who are accessible through devotion, accept this supreme and most sacred sacred thread (yajñopavīta), beautiful with nets of pure pearls and charming with golden threads. 12

O Lord Mṛtyuñjaya, O Sovereign Śrī, I constantly anoint all your limbs with this divine fragrance— blended with camphor and saffron, enriched with musk, prepared with Kālīya oil and cool water, and perfumed with Mandāra flowers— placed within a jewel-encrusted vessel that captivates the hearts of the gods.
With unbroken, white, divine grains properly combined with sesame seeds,
I worship you, O Mahādeva, conqueror of death, whose banner is the bull.
With *campaka*, lotus, *kurabaka*, *kunda*, *karavīra*, and *mallikā* flowers...

O Mṛtyuñjaya, O beloved of the lotus-eyed one, spread out your own crown. O Mṛtyuñjaya, place your two feet, which resemble beautiful lotuses, upon the pair of ruby sandals in the temple of the silent sage’s heart-lotus.

O Mṛtyuñjaya, I adorn my limbs with ruby armlets, crowns, and necklaces, with earrings set with gems upon my waistband, and with anklets and other ornaments that captivate the mind. With a pair of exceedingly pure chowries held by the shoulders of the elephant-faced one—
O Mortality-Conqueror, I meditate upon you within the lotus of my heart, who has caused the forest of worldly existence to fall away.

O Lord of the Gods, O Mortality-Conqueror, I offer to you this white parasol, as radiant as ten million moons, which bestows auspiciousness and is fitted with a golden handle; it is adorned with rubies and features golden pitchers set upon them.
O Mṛtyuñjaya, behold your own face, which resembles ten million gods of love, in a flawless jeweled mirror that stands as a true companion to the dense darkness of the three worlds.
(20) I shall offer camphor powder purified with browned clarified butter, together with kāleya.
I mentally conceive this lamp as the very body of Mṛtyuñjaya, arising from the sacred ground and perfumed with purifying incense.

O Lord of Gods, O Mṛtyuñjaya, this lamp of the bamboo-stand is provided with three wicks, possesses an unbroken and blazing flame that dispels both external and internal darkness, is accompanied by clarified butter, and is pleasing to the hearts of all the hosts of immortals.

O Lord Mṛtyuñjaya, beloved of Pārvatī, please partake of this royal food, which is sweet and delicate, served in a ruby bowl; it is accompanied by various auspicious vegetables seasoned with asafoetida, cumin, and black pepper, along with well-prepared leafy greens, cakes, and soup, all drenched in fresh ghee—may you eat this with the ritual water for rinsing the mouth (āpośana).
23. And there are the lovely fruits of kūṣmāṇḍa, vārtāka, paṭolikā, and kāravallī.
O Śrīkaṇṭha, O Mṛtyuñjaya, O Īśa, please partake of these well-cooked foods seasoned with saffron.
24 O Śiva, O Mṛtyuñjaya, O Lord, please take this water in between—it is cool, sweet, clear, purifying, fragrant, and light. 25
"Eat this unctuous milk-rice mixed with sugar, combined with cow's ghee and blended with plantain fruit—O Destroyer of Death!
It possesses supreme sweetness, being mixed with sugar and unctuous milks. (26)
O Lord Mṛtyuñjaya, who is united with the rays of the moon, partake of this supreme food.

O All-pervading One, O illustrious Mṛtyuñjaya, support of the three worlds, fill your vast belly with plantains, mangoes, wood-apples, and thorny fruits; with grapes, sweet dates, and pieces of sugarcane; with coconut water; and with honeyed jaggery-water, exquisitely scented with camphor. 27–28.
O Conqueror of Death, O one honored by the world, accept these pleasing pieces of plantain, which provide delight, along with mustard seeds, cumin, fragrant salt, and rock salt;
as well as this pure *āmalaka* fruit together with asafoetida and cumin, and this exceedingly sweet wood-apple (*kapittha*). (29)
O Mṛtyuñjaya, O Lord of the Universe, I offer this Bisakhanda mixed with salt to you.
O Mṛtyuñjaya, Lord of the Three Worlds, please partake of this rich rice-and-curd preparation accompanied by cardamom and ginger, served in a beautiful golden vessel as a substitute for nectar.
O Mṛtyuñjaya, O Śrī Karuṇāsamudra, suddenly partake of these soft side-dishes: ginger steeped in jambīra juice and charming pieces of unripe mango fruit.
[32] [Also partake of] that which is joined with asafoetida and cumin, beautifully prepared and filled with jambīra juice.
Drink this churned [milk] mixed with rock salt; O Conqueror of Death, destroyer of the sacrifice!

O Lord of the clouds, whose every desire is fulfilled, accept this glorious final sipping (ācamana) from the pure, holy waters of the Mandākinī, endowed with the fragrance of Mandāra flowers and golden lotuses.
With the pure waters of the celestial river flowing from the vessel of rubies held by Mṛtyuñjaya,
wash your pair of beautiful hands and feet, which are already filled with musk and sandalwood paste.
O Mahādeva, conqueror of death, perform the ritual sipping of water (ācamana) once more with the waters of the Ganges, perfumed by the *punnāga*, jasmine, and *kunda* flowers.
O Mṛtyuñjaya, I offer you betel-leaf mixed with pearl powder, scented with musk and camphor, and accompanied by areca nuts the color of gold. 37.
And I offer the Nīrājana, brilliant and raised high with sprouts of pure, glowing lamps.
With the resonance of the bell, I offer this to Mṛtyuñjaya, the destroyer of Tripura.

(38) O Lord, adorned with the king of serpents, saluted by the hosts of gods headed by Viriñci, and marked with the signs of the lotus, the fish, and the discus—I offer this once again at your lotus feet, O Mṛtyuñjaya. (39)
O Lord marked by Amṛtyuñjaya, I offer this handful of flowers— consisting of *puṇṇāga*, blue lotus, *kunda*, *jājī*, *mandāra* creepers, oleander, and lotuses— as well as *bilva* leaves and *tulasī*,
at every step, which cuts through all darkness and bestows all auspiciousness at every step.
With a heart full of devotion, I perform circumambulation; O Mṛtyuñjaya, protect me, protect me! 41. Salutations to the Lord of Gaurī, whose limbs are as white as crystal;
salutations, salutations to the Lord of the World, who is praised by the hosts of gods.
Salutations to Śrīkaṇṭha, and salutations again and again to the one who destroyed the city of the Daityas; salutations to Phālākṣa, and salutations to the destroyer of the intoxication of Smara. 42.
In this worldly existence, which is beset by various diseases and cries out under the threefold afflictions...

O Lord, O Śrī Mṛtyuñjaya, beloved of Pārvatī, Sovereign of All, always protect me with your compassionate gaze— me who am perpetually bound fast by the snares of wife and wealth, blinded by pride, and accompanied by a multitude of many sins.
In a palace made of jewels, within a bed strewn with fresh lotus petals and entirely covered with a beautiful white silk cloth,
there were two lovely pillows illuminated by the light of lamps scented with camphor.

I meditate upon Mṛtyuñjaya, whose feet are cherished by the lotus-hands of Pārvatī. (44) O man, if you perform worship with devotion—both internally within the lotus of the mind and externally with the forty desired, radiant offerings—at dawn, at night, and even at midday, you shall attain the glorious state of Mṛtyuñjaya, a station of manifold wonders. (45)
The worship of the five-syllabled mantra at the Linga of Umāpati yields heaven by its daily vision in the morning,
fruit equal to a horse-sacrifice at midday,
and liberation in the evening at the time of sunset and dusk.
Equal to the three periods of time, bestowing desired fruits, immediate, faultless, and firm.
Thus ends [the work] composed by the venerable Śaṅkara Bhagavat, the wandering ascetic teacher (parivrājaka-ācārya) and disciple of the venerable Govinda Bhagavat-pūjyapāda.
The Mṛtyuñjaya Mental Worship Hymn is complete.
